_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the scoring weights: the top-level performanceComposite that blends the four supplier sub-scores, plus two risk composites (performanceRisk, which feeds the composite's risk_score component, and supplyRisk, the Kraljic Y-axis). Extracted from python/scores.py (composite + performanceRisk) and python/compute_analyses.py (supplyRisk) so every per-component weight is now an EXPLICIT normalized weight. For the risk composites each component's response curve is normalized to 0-100 in code and the WEIGHT here scales it; weight * 100 == the old point ceiling (country_distance 0.60->60, roster_concentration 0.40->40; supply_concentration 0.50->50, cost_premium 0.25->25, import_friction 0.25->25). performanceComposite is WEIGHTS ONLY: its components (quality_score/delivery_score/process_score/risk_score) are the EXISTING sub-scores computed by scores.py, not formula-defined, so they carry builtin:true and the future formula editor must never offer to edit their formula. Weights per composite MUST sum to 1.0. invertPolarity is a COMPUTE flag (=true applies the final 100-minus, performanceRisk higher=safer); performanceComposite uses invertPolarity=false because it is a weighted average of higher-is-better sub-scores (combine_score's clip is then a no-op). polarityLabel is the DISPLAY badge copy and is authoritative for the UI — never re-derive the badge from invertPolarity (they are different concerns: a compute flag vs display text). configuredIn links a built-in sub-score to the composite that PRODUCES it (risk_score -> performanceRisk); the two weight sets MULTIPLY, not add. ID CONVENTION (deliberate, not sloppiness): performanceComposite component ids ARE the scores.py column names (quality_score, delivery_score, process_score, risk_score) because these components are not formula-defined — they ARE those columns, and the id documenting exactly which column it reads is a feature, not a mapping layer that could drift. The risk composite ids (supply_concentration, cost_premium, ...) are unsuffixed because they are not columns. Consumed by python/risk_config.py (binding; reads weight/enabled/invertPolarity only) and lib/risk-model.ts (types + loader). VERSIONING (Stage 2): each composite carries its OWN `version` (bumped on save only when THAT composite's own components change); `schemaVersion` is the file-format version, separate. Fingerprints are DERIVED (never stored) over COMPUTE-AFFECTING fields only (weights, enabled, invertPolarity, derived dependsOn) — shortLabel/polarityLabel/label/definition/version/_comment are excluded, so a fingerprint change means the numbers changed. The printed report footer stamps the schema version + ALL per-composite versions + one whole-config fingerprint (a fingerprint is only comparable within one schemaVersion, which records the fingerprint's compute-affecting scope). Defaults live in config/risk-model.defaults.json (the reset-to-defaults target; keep in sync with the shipped weights here). Do NOT change weights without re-recording every affected baseline in the same change. LOOKUP TABLES (Stage A): the geographic + concentration lookups that used to be hardcoded in python/scores.py and python/compute_analyses.py now live in the top-level `lookupTables` block; a formula-defined component reaches one through its formula's variables -- a `lookup` variable declares `table` (see the FORMULAS + VARIABLES and PREREQUISITE P sections; the per-component `lookupTable` field this originally used was DROPPED in P). `concentration_curve` is SHARED by supplyRisk.supply_concentration AND performanceRisk.roster_concentration (one definition, two consumers -- editing it moves BOTH scores). country_distance and import_friction are deliberately SEPARATE tables (geography vs trade-agreement coverage). Each table carries key->value `rows` (with `members` = country codes for the geographic tables), an explicit REQUIRED `default`, and values validated to [0,100] at load. Read by python/risk_config.py (lookup_numeric / lookup_country) so scores.py and compute_analyses.py share ONE loader; table values are in the compute-affecting fingerprint scope (Stage 2), so editing the shared curve moves both consumers' compositeFingerprints. Adding lookup values to that scope EXPANDED the fingerprint's coverage, so schemaVersion moved 2.0.0->2.1.0 in the SAME change (commit fa7d75f): a fingerprint is only comparable within one schemaVersion, and a 2.0.0 vs 2.1.0 fingerprint differs at identical weights (RISK_MODEL_FINGERPRINT became e4db2d7e) WITHOUT any number changing. TABLE VERSIONING (Stage B): each lookup table carries its OWN `version`, bumped when THAT table is edited. A table edit moves its consumers' FINGERPRINTS but NOT their versions -- a shared table is no composite's own knob, so version stays per-editable-object and the fingerprint carries the transitive effect (same principle as composites). Table versions live in the config + the settings UI, NOT the report footer (which stays one line: schema + composite versions + whole-config fingerprint; the git-tracked config resolves a fingerprint to an exact historical state). `input` is STRUCTURE, never editable. count tables keep a contiguous 0..N key domain (a hole would silently fall through to `default`); country tables require DISJOINT members across rows (else the country->row match is order-dependent). Table defaults (the reset target) live in config/risk-model.defaults.json under `lookupTables`. FORMULAS + VARIABLES (Stage D): the lookup/computed components are now formula-defined -- each carries a `formula` (whitelisted arithmetic over `variables` ids) + `bounds` {lo,hi} applied to the result (0-100 by construction). The `variables` catalogue is the namespace: each entry is a per-supplier scalar RESOLVED OUTSIDE the evaluator and injected as env[id]. A `lookup` variable declares `table` + `key` (the source field: `country` or the derived `roster_other_count`); its missing/unknown-key default is the TABLE's own `default` row (single-source, NOT re-declared on the variable). A `computed` variable (cost_premium) declares an explicit `default` (0.0, neutral-when-absent) since it has no table. supply_concentration + roster_concentration are DELIBERATELY two ids on the SAME (table,key) -- one signal under two names, NOT merged, because they are two distinct COMPONENTS in two composites (the r=-0.852 correlation between the two scores follows from this shared resolver); risk_config.validate_variables asserts they stay the same (table,key) so the signal cannot be silently split. The existing components are single-atom formulas (formula = the component's own variable id, bounds 0-100), so the re-expression is byte-identical (normalize_to_bounds is a x1.0 identity at (0,100)). python/formula_eval.py is THE evaluator; risk_config.evaluate_composite iterates components in DECLARED ORDER (float addition is not associative, so order is part of the identity). PREREQUISITE P (schema 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0, commit 897bbba): DONE. `component.lookupTable` (Stage A/B) was DROPPED -- table references are now DERIVED through formula -> variables -> table (lib/risk-model.componentTableRefs / consumersOfTable; python/risk_config resolves the same way at compute time), so a composed formula reading MULTIPLE tables is representable where one lookupTable field was not. The compute-affecting fingerprint was EXTENDED to cover, per formula-defined component, its `formula` + `bounds` + the specs of the variables it references (a lookup's kind/key/table; a computed's resolver/default) + the resolved content of every lookup table those variables read (projectComponentFormula). So editing a formula, a bound, a variable spec, or a shared table now MOVES the fingerprint -- closing the reproducibility hole BEFORE Stage F makes formulas user-editable. Referenced tables are serialized SORTED BY table id (deterministic regardless of the order variables appear in the formula; guarded by scripts/fingerprint_check.ts). This scope expansion is why schemaVersion moved 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0: at IDENTICAL weights the 2.1.0 fingerprint (e4db2d7e) and the 2.2.0 fingerprint differ WITHOUT any score changing (RISK_MODEL_FINGERPRINT became d3aa19ab). The (table,key) same-signal guard for supply_concentration / roster_concentration still fails loudly (risk_config.validate_variables). STAGE E (schema 2.2.0 -> 2.3.0): the variable CATALOGUE expanded from 5 to 12 usable entries. NEW `aggregate`-kind variables declare a `source` (snake_case PO column) + `agg` (risk_config.AGG_FUNCS) resolved by scores.build_aggregate_map to {supplier_id -> float} at supplier grain -- adding one is a CONFIG edit, no new resolver. Each entry carries `feedsBuiltin` (the builtin sub-score it is an input to, or absent) + `eta2` {category,country} (measured one-way-ANOVA discrimination via scripts/measure_catalogue_eta.py; DISPLAY/flag metadata only, NOT compute-affecting -- high eta2 is not a gate, country tier legitimately IS country). DOUBLE-COUNT BLOCK (structural + graph-derived, NOT a warning): a variable feeding a builtin sub-score is BLOCKED in any composite that produces a SIBLING builtin -- concretely builtin-input variables are blocked in performanceRisk (risk_config.validate_builtin_input_block / lib.builtinInputBlockedIn, both derived from configuredIn); they are ALLOWED in supplyRisk (the standalone Kraljic Y-axis, which never feeds performanceComposite) with a UI design note only. `aggregate` source/agg ARE compute-affecting (projectComponentFormula projects them), so schemaVersion moved 2.2.0 -> 2.3.0; the shipped fingerprint is UNCHANGED (d3aa19ab) because no shipped formula references an aggregate variable yet. PREREQUISITE — ADD-COMPONENT ON performanceComposite (DEFERRED, NOT built): adding a non-builtin (formula) component to performanceComposite is a CORE scoring-path change, not an extension of the risk-composite mechanism, because performanceComposite is WEIGHTS-ONLY — scores.py combines the four builtin sub-score COLUMNS by weight (sum(m[col]*weight)) and does NOT blend through risk_config.evaluate_composite the way supplyRisk/performanceRisk do. Deferred deliberately: the realistic need (the organisation drops a dimension) is already served by DISABLING a builtin (which renormalizes correctly via resolve_effective_weights), and a genuinely new fifth dimension is speculative. Add is excluded on performanceComposite today via the per-component builtin flag (every component is builtin). Before enabling add/remove of non-builtin components here, THREE things must land TOGETHER: (1) compute_scores must route performanceComposite through evaluate_composite, with the builtin sub-score columns (quality_score/delivery_score/process_score/risk_score) entering the env as variables, so builtin and formula components blend through ONE path rather than two; (2) the double-count guard (risk_config.validate_builtin_input_block / lib.builtinInputBlockedIn) must be extended from the TRANSITIVE case (a builtin-input variable in a composite that PRODUCES a sibling builtin, e.g. performanceRisk feeding risk_score) to the DIRECT SIBLING case (a builtin-input variable in a component sitting directly alongside that builtin in performanceComposite — on_time_rate there double-counts delivery_score at 0.30, more directly than the transitive case); (3) python/preview.py must accept performanceComposite as a candidate composite and report PERFORMANCE ZONE movement, not Kraljic quadrant movement (today it KeyErrors on 'formula' because the builtin components carry none). The guard is deliberately NOT pre-extended: with no add there is no live sibling case, and this project does not build for cases that cannot occur (same precedent as the vacuous componentReferrers orphan check).

concentration_curve.label: Roster concentration curve
concentration_curve.definition: SHARED step curve on the number of OTHER suppliers in the same category across the full roster (active or not); fewer alternatives -> higher risk. Values are the normalized 0-100 axis (the old 0-50 points doubled: 50->100, 35->70, 22->44, 12->24, 5->10; the x2 that used to live in scores.concentration_0_100 is folded in here, bit-identical). Referenced by BOTH supplyRisk.supply_concentration AND performanceRisk.roster_concentration -- ONE definition, TWO consumers; editing it moves both scores, and is why the two risk scores correlate r=-0.852 (documented on the Methodology page). `input`=count: keyed by the integer other-in-category count; anything not listed (>=5, true abundance) falls through to `default` 0.

country_distance.label: Country distance tiers
country_distance.definition: Geographic supply-distance tier of the supplier's country (0 = domestic, 100 = far). Consumed by performanceRisk.country_distance. Deliberately SEPARATE from import_friction (geography, not trade blocs): India (IN) sits at 60 here (Asia-Pacific by geography) but at 100 on import_friction (outside RCEP since 2019) -- the divergence is intentional; do not unify. `input`=country: matched by ISO alpha-2 code (also full name for ID); any code in no row's `members` falls through to `default` 100.

import_friction.label: Import friction tiers
import_friction.definition: Indonesia trade-agreement coverage of the supplier's country (0 = domestic, 100 = no agreement). Consumed by supplyRisk.import_friction. Deliberately SEPARATE from country_distance (trade blocs, not geography): India is outside RCEP so lands at 100 here despite being Asia-Pacific (60) on distance. `input`=country: matched by ISO alpha-2 code (also IDN / full name for ID); any code in no row's `members` falls through to `default` 100.

cycle_time.label: Total cycle time (PR to payment, days)

payment_days_past_terms.label: Payment days past terms
payment_days_past_terms.locked: Inert — a uniform random draw on {0..15}; nothing explains its variance (Methodology dead-metrics).

payment_date.label: Payment date
payment_date.locked: Outside window scope — the reporting window anchors on order date (poDate), not payment date.

requisition_estimate.label: Requisition estimate accuracy
requisition_estimate.locked: Generator artifact — the estimate is the order value jittered by Uniform(-0.10, +0.15), a copy of the outcome, not a forecast.

cycle_time_cv.label: Cycle-time variability (CV)
cycle_time_cv.locked: Measured dead — ~93% determined by category (eta-squared 0.94); re-reports buying method, not supplier conduct.

delivery_variability.label: Delivery variability
delivery_variability.locked: Measured — no forward signal; the on-time boolean is a coin flip at the global rate.

components.label: Quality
components.definition: Existing quality sub-score: per-PO defect rate + complaint rate, each normalized 0-100 against fixed bounds, averaged. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Delivery
components.definition: Existing delivery sub-score: on-time-delivery % + average lead time, each normalized 0-100 against fixed bounds, averaged. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Process
components.definition: Existing process sub-score: three-way-match pass rate, normalized 0-100. Computed by scores.py from transaction data; a built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Risk
components.definition: The performanceRisk composite output (structural: country distance + roster concentration, inverted so higher=safer). A built-in sub-score, not a formula-editable component.

components.label: Country distance
components.definition: Geographic supply-distance tier of the supplier's country. 0-100 lookup {Indonesia:0, ASEAN:30, Asia-Pacific:60, other:100}.

components.label: Roster concentration
components.definition: Roster-based supply concentration (the SAME curve as supplyRisk.supply_concentration), on the 0-100 axis {0:100,1:70,2:44,3:24,4:10,>=5:0}.

components.label: Supply concentration
components.definition: Step curve on the number of OTHER suppliers in the same category across the full roster (active or not); fewer alternatives -> higher risk. Normalized curve {0:100,1:70,2:44,3:24,4:10,>=5:0}.

components.label: Cost premium
components.definition: Spend-weighted item-price premium vs the cross-supplier benchmark, over supplier x item pairs with >=2 POs where the item has >=2 suppliers. Normalized clip(premium*250, 0, 100); at/below market -> 0.

components.label: Import friction
components.definition: Indonesia trade-agreement coverage of the supplier's country. Normalized {domestic:0, AFTA:32, RCEP-non-ASEAN:64, other:100}.
